svg.title: Complete two-mode controls expose a higher-energy minimum family and a negative comparison.
svg.desc: English: Complete two-mode controls expose a higher-energy minimum family and a negative comparison. 繁體中文：完整兩模態控制呈現較高能量極小值家族及負面對照。

cc:Work.dc:description: Energy ordering in the independently certified, complete zero-phase M=2 controls. Panels (a,b) separate the ZIP and prior-study nonlinear coefficient sets, with their own energy scales. Black and orange curves give the lowest and highest energies among strict minima; blue triangles give the highest retained optimizer minimum energy. The ZIP model develops a higher-energy local-minimum family, while the prior coefficient set can retain only one signed-pair energy. Panel (c) explicitly displays highest-minus-lowest minimum energy, using blue for ZIP and orange for prior coefficients; zero records intentional upper-panel coincidence. The highest-minimum envelope can jump when a new minimum enters the set; that is not an energy discontinuity along a connected branch. Certification is limited to the specified two-mode polynomial, not a continuum global-minimum claim. Energy differences between minima are not transition barriers. Missing optimizer minima remain missing, not zero. Every plotted state passed original-gradient verification and Hessian classification. This control does not imply the same ordering for every phase or truncation.
